title: Cable Fly
summary: Standing cable fly: bring the handles together in front of the chest. Chest 1, with a steady pull through the whole range.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: cable station with an adjustable pulley.

muscles.why: The pecs bring the upper arm across the body (horizontal adduction). With mid-height cables, the line favors the mid/lower chest (1) over the upper chest (0.7).
The front delts help bring the arm forward: minor.

setup.text: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height.
Take a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance.
Slight bend in the elbows; arms open with a stretch across the chest.

form_cues.cue: Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows
form_cues.why: Hugging motion, arc not press, keeps the work on the chest.

form_cues.cue: Open wide to a deep chest stretch
form_cues.why: A fixed elbow bend stops it turning into a press.

form_cues.cue: Bring hands together in a hugging arc
form_cues.why: The hands meeting in front is the chest's shortest point.

form_cues.cue: Keep the elbow bend fixed. This is a hug, not a press.
form_cues.why: Pulley height sets which part of the chest the line of pull favors.

bias_tweaks.change: Pulleys low, pull up and in (low-to-high)
bias_tweaks.effect: The line follows the upper chest fibers.

bias_tweaks.change: Pulleys high, pull down and in (high-to-low)
bias_tweaks.effect: The line follows the lower chest fibers.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Bending and straightening the elbows so it turns into a press.
mistakes.fix: Lighten the load until the elbow bend stays the same throughout.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbows bend more to press it.
Losing the stretch by stepping too far forward.
mistakes.fix: Stand where the arms can open fully.

misconceptions.reality: The pec can't be trained 'inner' or 'outer'; flies train the chest through a big range with low fatigue.

misconceptions.myth: Machines don't build muscle like free weights.
misconceptions.reality: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth in a meta-analysis. Pick by fit, stability and how well you can push close to failure.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Easy to push close to failure; stop when the elbows start bending more.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Machine fly with the most tension where the arms meet.
Low-to-high cable path for the upper chest.
Dumbbell fly: tension is highest in the stretch, light at the top.
A press: more load, plus front delts and triceps.

notes: Fly variations have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
